newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise wins Turkey water contract.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise wins Turkey water contract.

text.p: French water and utilities company Lyonnaise des Eaux said on Tuesday it signed a water management contract for the southern Turkish city of Antalya.

A Lyonnaise spokesman said it was the first time a Turkish municipality had delegated a water management contract to a private sector firm. Turnover in the first year of the 10-year contract will be $7 million, he added.

The contract was signed on Monday by Lyonnaise and the Turkish ENKA group, represented by their 50/50 joint venture Antsu. The deal will not require significant investment by Lyonnaise as it is funded by the World Bank and the EIB.
The water management deal was a significant win for Lyonnaise as the Turkish market offers great potential, the spokesman said.
Antalya's population is normally 530,000 and expands to one million in the holiday season. Its resident population is expected to grow to one million by 2005.

Lyonnaise is represented in Turkey with an office run by its Degremont subsidiary, which last year won contracts to build two water treatment plants worth 58 million and 55 million francs, respectively.
